name: Queue-Gated Mouse-Scrub Video Kinematics & Hardware Anti-Flood Seeking
description: Interactive video timeline architecture that smoothly scrubs video playback via horizontal mouse velocity. Solves video decoder freeze and frame-drop through an asynchronous onSeeked queue latch that buffers target time mutations without flooding the hardware decoder.
designPhilosophy: Transforming passive video backgrounds into responsive tactile storytelling where the user physically scrubs video time via horizontal mouse velocity. Solves the catastrophic decoder frame-drop and latency stutter caused by rapid video.currentTime mutations by implementing an asynchronous onSeeked queue latch.
appropriateUseCases: Creative agency interactive hero sections and digital studio showreels
3D product turnaround viewers and automotive 360-degree interactive showcases
Architectural walkthroughs and cinematic portfolio backgrounds
Interactive fashion lookbooks and editorial video timelines
implementationApproach: 1. Delta Motion Tracking: On window mousemove, track horizontal velocity delta: deltaX = currentX - prevX. 2. Time Offset Formula: timeDelta = (deltaX / window.innerWidth) * SENSITIVITY * video.duration where SENSITIVITY = 0.8. 3. Boundary Clamping: targetTime = Math.min(Math.max(targetTime + timeDelta, 0), video.duration). 4. Anti-Flood Queue Latch: Maintain an isSeeking boolean flag. If isSeeking is false, immediately set video.currentTime = targetTime and set isSeeking = true. If true, buffer targetTime. 5. onSeeked Resolution: When the HTML5 video fires 'seeked', if targetTime has moved during the seek operation, immediately trigger the next seek to the buffered time; otherwise set isSeeking = false. 6. Video Configuration: preload='auto', muted, playsInline, object-fit: cover.
performanceConsiderations: Prevents browser hardware video decoders from queue-flooding, which drops frames and spikes GPU memory. Reduces seek requests by up to 85% during rapid pointer gestures.
accessibilityRequirements: Under prefers-reduced-motion, mouse-scrubbing is completely disabled; the video displays a static poster frame or plays at a gentle ambient 0.5x speed with visible pause/play controls.
